## A short version of the work

My strongest work has one theme: take a noisy, high-friction problem and turn it into a system that can gather evidence, make a decision, and keep going.

That has taken me from chatbots at a major bank, to branded AR products, to autonomous research and developer tools. The stack changes. The standard does not: a useful result should be observable, reproducible, and usable.

## Three things worth opening

### 01 — Paperclaw

**The question:** how much of the solar capacity promoted around Berlin actually exists?

**What I made:** an always-on agent that combines the official registry with Sentinel-2 satellite imagery, tracks 571 registered parks, and separates verified generation assets from projects that exist only on paper.

**Why it was technically interesting:** the difficult part was not one model call. It was keeping a changing source of evidence coherent: retrieval, geospatial checks, ranking, alerting, and a public presentation of what the system believes.

[Explore the live monitor](https://metaphysicist1.github.io/papercrawl/) · [Read the repository](https://github.com/Metaphysicist1/papercrawl)

---

### 02 — Relay

**The question:** what happens when a software task is divided before one coding agent becomes the bottleneck?

**What I made:** a parallel agent workflow that takes one prompt and runs work across isolated git worktrees, giving separate agents their own branch and preventing changes from being mixed together too early.

**What I learned:** parallelism is only useful with boundaries. Execution, review, merge decisions, and access to the repository need to be designed separately.

[View the repository](https://github.com/Metaphysicist1/relay)

---

### 03 — UniMate

**The question:** could a confusing admissions process become something a student can actually navigate?

**What I made:** an AI companion for German university admissions, focused on turning scattered requirements into clear next steps.

**Live proof:** [unimate.study](https://unimate.study) · [Source](https://github.com/Metaphysicist1/unimate)
